trace.claim: The paper investigates whether online political hostility is associated with political engagement and its antecedents.
Online political hostility is positively associated with several indicators of political engagement and its antecedents.
The study uses a dataset combining two years of survey and behavioral data from X/Twitter users.
Political engagement indicators are positively associated with online political hostility.
The association between engagement and hostility is stronger among users with higher levels of affective polarization.
Hostile users are more active and have greater potential reach on X/Twitter.
The study does not establish causal relationships between political engagement and online hostility.
The paper extends classical theories of political engagement to include the potential for online political hostility.
Classical theories of political behavior emphasize the positive democratic role of political engagement.
